content: US Investment Grade: The pullback in equities also weighed on credit, with US IG spreads ending the week 1bp wider, resulting in excess returns of -0.1%. Spread curves bear-steepened while better rated bonds underperformed. Telecoms, technology, utilities delivered the weakest excess returns, while basic industry and services held up better. US IG funds saw $3.6bn of net inflows last week, lifting YTD inflows to +$69bn. Primary market activity was robust, with $47bn of bonds pricing last week. YTD supply is tracking at $1,095bn (+26% YoY).

US Leveraged Credit: HY spreads widened by 7bp, translating into excess returns of -0.1%. Loans delivered positive total returns at 0.05% last week, outperforming HY (-0.4%). The moves were accompanied by decompression across HY and Loans. Within HY, telecom and consumer goods underperformed, while energy and technology held in better. HY funds reported net inflows of $880mn (-$6.2bn YTD), while loan funds saw net inflows of $760mn last week (+$3.5bn YTD). Both HY and Loans recorded $13bn of issuance last week. YTD issuance now stands at $160bn (+42% YoY) in HY and $188bn (-3% YoY) in loans.

EU Investment Grade: European credit outperformed the US last week with spreads tightening by 3bp, resulting in excess returns of +0.1%. Curves bull-flattened, while BBBs saw slight outperformance across ratings. Media outperformed, while transportation and basic industry lagged. European IG fund inflows rose to ~$700m (0.1% of AUM) following last week's more muted but positive print (~$155m). The inflows were heavily skewed towards ETFs, while mutual funds reported small net outflows. Issuance moderated to €12bn last week, lifting YTD volumes to €378bn (flat YoY).

EU High Yield: EU HY outperformed IG, with spreads tightening by 13bp last week resulting in excess returns of +0.4%. However, the moves were most pronounced in BBs, while performance was more mixed further down the ratings spectrum. Leisure and tech outperformed, while telecoms and real estate lagged. European HY fund net inflows rose to ~$425mln / 0.4% of AUM, with both mutual funds and ETFs saw net inflows. YTD supply is tracking at €67bn (+11% YoY).

Key Trades: We reiterate our key trade recommendations across sectors in IG that we outlined in our Mid-Year Outlooks. In the US, we are overweight banks, utilities, while technology/hyperscalers remain our key underweights. In Europe, we like banks, energy, and defensives, while we recommend an underweight on cyclical sectors, autos in particular. In Asia, we like Japan Banks TLAC Senior debt and unhedged AUD LC Corp bonds.

Credit Derivatives: Synthetic spreads widened across the US and EU, with CDX IG and iTraxx Main ending the week 2bp and 1bp wider, respectively, while HY/Xover underperformed. While implied volatility ticked up from the YTD lows, credit lagged the rise in equities vol.

Asia Credit: Asia Credit spreads tightened by 2bp over the last week, while APAC Credit spreads remained flat. In Asia credit, Asia HY (-18bp) outperformed Asia IG (-2bp). Similarly, in APAC credit, HY spreads tightened by 3bp while IG spreads were flat.

Key Trades Across Sectors in IG
- Hyperscaler capex expectations remain extremely elevated (> $1.1tr in 2027), with capital intensity still rising and likely underestimated by consensus, reinforcing heavy issuance outlook.

- In addition to heavy issuance, we also note that capacity in non-USD markets to fund this is limited, and effective leverage is rising for hyperscalers via off-balance-sheet channels, which increases risks around overbuild and weaker-than-expected earnings over time.
- These factors skew risk/reward negatively for IG tech, with potential spread widening and asymmetric downside for credit vs. equities.
HQ hyperscalers have only modestly underperformed so far

US IG – OW Banks, Especially Regional Banks

- Maintain OW on Banks (especially Regionals), with scope for spread compression after modest YTD underperformance, supported by a more constructive regulatory backdrop and ~$291bn of excess capital (+28%) according to our equity analysts.
- Bank issuance remains largely opportunistic vs. structural, with continued support from a resilient and diversified M&A pipeline.

US IG - OW Utilities, Especially Hybrids
- Utilities offer a compelling way to express AI-driven power demand, benefiting from rising data center load and underappreciated upside to power prices, particularly for IPPs.

- Capex is rising but remains more manageable than hyperscalers, with strong fundamentals supporting absorption of higher issuance and attractive compensation, especially lower in the capital structure.

- Banks remain our key overweight: The sector continues to show historically strong fundamentals and a supportive earnings backdrop aided by steep curves, accelerating M&A and primary market activity, while the sector also faces fewer supply pressures compared to corporates. We continue to see better risk-adjusted valuations in banks, particularly further down the capital structure. The key risk is a sharp deterioration in the macro outlook that could weigh on the sector.

- Still see value in Energy: Rising oil prices have tended to lead to an outperformance of the sector in IG. Our broad rule of thumb is that for every 10% rise in Brent, oil and gas sector spreads tend to outperform the index by ~3bp. So far, the energy sector has lagged the rise in oil prices, leaving room for further outperformance. A key risk to this view is a sharp decline in oil prices.

EU IG – UW Cyclicals, Particularly Autos

- Autos exposed to structural challenges: Over recent years, European autos' profitability has been under intensifying pressure, with structural headwinds of a margin dilutive EV mix, intensifying competition from Chinese automakers, and inflation putting pressure on affordability. Against this backdrop, 25% tariffs and the Middle East conflict induced oil price shock add further headwinds to already historically low margins and high investment. The headwinds are particularly pronounced for volume OEMs as our equity analysts highlight (European OEMs: 2026 getting darker).

- While most OEMs are operating with low leverage, the broader challenges are increasingly reflected in a gradually deteriorating ratings mix in the sector, and the sector remains skewed to more negative ratings outlooks / watches than the broader market.

- However, credit markets have priced out much of the downside, with the sector spread relative to the index now back at 11bp, just 5bp away from the long-run median, and well below recent peaks. In the scenario of a quick de-escalation in the Middle East, autos would likely outperform, but we recommend selling into that relief rally.

Asia Credit – Long Japan Banks Senior TLAC

- In Despite the recent tightening in Japan banks senior TLAC spreads, its is still 10bps winder than its year-to-date tights. We understand investors' concerns surrounding supply risk for Japan banks senior TLAC.

• However, at close to double Asia IG spreads, we believe Japan bank senior TLAC compensates investors for supply-risk concerns. In addition, Japan banks senior TLAC also benefit from the strong inflows into US credit funds, which have Japan credit in their mandates.

• Lastly, we believe that higher JGB yield risk is manageable for Japanese banks and is unlikely to put pressure on its TLAC spread (see Thought #1: USD bond-issuing Japan banks' exposure to JGB risk is manageable, January 23, 2026).
Japan Banks Senior TLAC spread pickup over Asia IG is the highest since 2023
Asia Credit – Long Unhedged AUD LC Corp Bonds

- Our global FX strategy team is bullish on the AUD as its medium-term outlook has improved. Their year-end target for USDAUD is 0.75 by end of the year, which translates into ~ 5% FX returns for USD-based investors.
- Aside from the FX alpha opportunity provided by this trade, the carry return from AUD LC corps bonds looks attractive as well.
• AUD LC corps bonds currently offer close to a 100bp yield pick-up over Asia IG.
